note: Ranges and default values for the controls, with the basis for each default. A default of null means the value, and the note on where it comes from, are taken from the data files. Values are fractions: 0.02 means 2%. Defaults marked illustrative are starting values for exploring scenarios, not estimates.

centralBankLimit.basis: Illustrative assumption. The highest in this data is the Bank of Japan's 47% in 2024.

capLevel.basis: Illustrative assumption, one value for every country. Under Volcker the US 10-year yield was above 10% every year from 1980 to 1985, peaking above 15% in 1981, and the Federal Reserve did not cap it.

selloffResponse.basis: Illustrative assumption, five times the usual yield response.

runoff.basis: Illustrative assumption: with no runoff the central bank keeps its share of the debt.

yieldResponse.basis: Illustrative assumption, one value for every country: about 3 basis points of yield for each point of GDP, in the range of published estimates of the effect of government debt on long-term yields (about 2 to 4 basis points; Engen and Hubbard 2004, Laubach 2009).

priceSensitive.note: A group's default comes from the country's data file where the data separates holders by type. Otherwise it is the illustrative value here.

foreign.basis: Illustrative assumption for countries whose data cannot separate foreign official from foreign private holders.
